welcome.title: Welcome to your diary!
welcome.body: This home page sums up your season. A short tour to see the essentials? (Esc to skip it.)

today.title: Note an event
today.body: Click today's date, or its pen, to note a training, a competition, a strength session… You'll fill in its sheet afterwards.

calendar.title: Your calendar
calendar.body: This month and the next, with an icon per event. Click it to see the whole season at a glance.

regularity.title: Your regularity
regularity.body: Number of days you noted a session since the journal began, and your weeks in a row with at least two sessions. Something to keep you going!

competitions.title: FFTA competitions
competitions.body: The invitations published in your departments, and “Plan” to choose your season's competitions on a map. One click adds them to your journal.

export.title: Journal publication
export.body: Print your season's diary: decorated calendars, sheets, photos and indicators, to keep the memory of this archery season.

tabs.title: The diary's sections
tabs.body: These tabs, like the sticky notes at the bottom of the page, lead to the Journal, the Sheets, the Stats and your Profile. Each has its own short tour the first time you open it.

account.title: Your account
account.body: Open your account to add a new journal or rate the app.

help.title: Replay the tour
help.body: Not sure? The “?” button replays the tour of the page shown, whenever you like. On a phone, it is in your account's menu.

welcome.title: Your month's journal
welcome.body: Here is your season month by month: your sessions, their description sheets, and a calendar to decorate. A quick tour? (Escape to skip it.)

calendar.title: The calendar
calendar.body: Click a day to add or plan a session (training, competition, coaching…). If the icon is greyed out, its description sheet is still to complete. An “FFTA” ticket marks the day's competitions.

new-event.title: New event
new-event.body: The “+” adds an event on the date of your choice: training, competition, strength work, or one of your own types.

navigate.title: Changing month
navigate.body: To get around faster, use the “Today” button, or the calendar one to show the whole season.

summary.title: The month at a glance
summary.body: The arrows shot this month, and your satisfaction: click the stars to rate it.

share.title: Share the month
share.body: Your month written in chalk on a blackboard, ready for Instagram.

decor.title: The decoration
decor.body: Pick a decoration for this month, and the colour the month's name is shown in.

coloring.title: Colouring
coloring.body: Colour the decoration as you like, or let “Colour automatically” do it.

legend.title: The legend
legend.body: To recall what each icon means.

welcome.title: Your indicators
welcome.body: Your filled-in sheets turn into figures and charts, to follow your progress. A quick tour? (Escape to skip it.)

period.title: The period
period.body: The indicators cover a journal's period, or everything you have noted since the start.

season.title: The season summary
season.body: The whole season summed up on a whiteboard: best scores, averages per arrow, goals reached… to share on Instagram.

goals.title: Your goals
goals.body: Set yourself goals, then note the day you reach them.

rankings.title: National rankings
rankings.body: Your place in the FFTA rankings for your bow and category, this season and the one before. It needs your licence number, category and bow (Profile page).

charts.title: The charts
charts.body: Arrows, durations, scores, averages per arrow, events, feelings: each card has its chart, often with buttons on top to change the span or the discipline.

favorite.title: Your favourite indicator
favorite.body: A card's star features it on the home page. One at a time.

welcome.title: Your binder of sheets
welcome.body: Here you keep what doesn't change from one session to the next: your technique, your settings, your strength programmes and your mental preparation. A quick tour?

binder.title: Four parts
binder.body: The binder has four half-pages, each with its colour. Each opens on the index of its sheets: a click on a title opens the sheet.

add.title: Adding a sheet
add.body: Each part's “+” creates a sheet: a title and, if you like, a ready-made template (“My string”, “My arrows”…) whose preview you see. The sheet then opens to be filled in.

technique.title: Technique
technique.body: Your technique points, cues and drills. These sheets can also keep up to 4 photos: a posture, an anchor, a drill.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body: Your bow, arrows, string and sight marks: write them down to find a setting that worked.

strength.title: Strength
strength.body: Build your strength sessions in a few clicks: the exercise, the sets, the repetitions or duration, the load and the rest. A strength session in the journal can then take that programme and tick each exercise done.

mental.title: Mental preparation
mental.body: Your shot routine, your key phrases, how you prepare a competition: to read again before shooting.

welcome.title: Your profile
welcome.body: Here is what the diary needs to know about you, and the people you share it with. A quick tour? (Escape to skip it.)

guests.title: Invitation
guests.body: Invite your archer friends so they start their own journal, and your coach so they see your current season's journal and, if you allow it, propose sessions and comment on yours.

competitions.title: Your competitions
competitions.body: Pick up to five departments: their FFTA competitions show in your calendars. Your home town gives the distance on the competitions' map.

configuration.title: Your configuration
configuration.body: Licence, name, category, bow and disciplines: they are used for competitions, rankings and finding your score sheets.

personalization.title: Personalisation
personalization.body: Choose your calendars' handwriting: a calligraphy, or a simpler font to read.

emails.title: Your emails
emails.body: Get your coach's news and a reminder in the week of your competitions. They can be turned off anytime.

calendar-feed.title: Your phone's calendar
calendar-feed.body: A link to add to your calendar: your sessions and competitions show up there by themselves.

welcome.title: The session sheet
welcome.body: Everything about your session: before, what you plan; after, your review. A quick tour? (Escape to skip it.)

info.title: The details
info.body: Date, duration, place, discipline and distance are noted ahead; arrows, score and, outdoors, the weather once the day has come.

photos.title: Photos
photos.body: Up to four photos per session: your target face, your gear, the shooting line… They stay private.

objective.title: The objective
objective.body: What you want to work on during this session.

steps.title: The outline
steps.body: The “+” adds a step (in minutes or arrows). On the day, tick those you have done.

review.title: The review
review.body: After the session: your satisfaction and technique, then your analysis, what to keep, to improve and for next time.

feelings.title: Your feelings
feelings.body: How you felt, physically and mentally: they feed the indicators.

save.title: Save
save.body: Remember to save your changes before closing the sheet.

again.title: Do this session again
again.body: A new session, on another day, with the same programme.

share.title: Share
share.body: Your session as an Instagram card, with the details and photos of your choice.

home.welcomeBody: MyArcheryDiary is your archery notebook, always at hand. Like a real notebook lying on your desk, it keeps track of every session: training, coaching, competitions and strength work. At the end of the season, generate your notebook as a PDF to print or share it.

audience.question: Who is MyArcheryDiary for?
audience.answer: Archers of every level who want to keep track of their practice, and their coaches: an archer invites their coach, who then follows their journal of the current season. At the end of the season, the archer can generate their notebook as a PDF to print or share it.

start.question: How do I get started?
start.answer: Create an account with your email or Google, then open your first journal. All that is left is to write down your sessions.

journal.question: What is a journal?
journal.answer: A period you name, usually a season. It gathers the events dated within that period in a calendar you can decorate and colour month by month.

events.question: What can I write down?
events.answer: Training, coaching, competitions and strength work, plus four types of your own. Each event has its sheet: scores, arrow count, self-assessment, feelings, photos, and the weather when shooting outdoors.

planning.question: Can I plan my sessions ahead?
planning.answer: Yes: for a day to come, note the duration, place, discipline, distance, goal and the session's outline, step by step. On the day, tick the steps done, then fill in the review. “Do this session again” creates a new one with the same programme, and your coach can suggest some too.

competitions.question: How do I find competitions?
competitions.answer: Choose your departments on the Profile page: the FFTA competitions of your disciplines show in your calendars, with the published invitations on the home page. The “Competition planning” window also shows them on a map, with the distance from your starting town; one click adds them to your journal, and their results open from the sheet once published.

progress.question: Where can I see my progress?
progress.answer: The Stats page shows your scores, your average per arrow at each distance, your arrow volume and your feelings, next to the goals you set yourself. The home page follows your regularity, and the “Season summary” sums up a whole season.

share.question: Can I share my season?
share.answer: Yes: each past session and your season summary can be posted on Instagram as a card, and “Journal publication” gathers calendars, indicators and sheets in a PDF to print or keep.

devices.question: On which devices?
devices.answer: Phone, tablet or computer, in your browser, in French or English. You can also add it to your phone's home screen and open it like an app.

PLANK_FRONT.description: On your forearms and toes, the body straight like a board.
PLANK_FRONT.tips:
Elbows under the shoulders.
Hips in line: neither sagging nor raised.
Draw your navel in and breathe calmly.

PLANK_SIDE.description: On your side, on one forearm and the edge of the foot, the body in line.
PLANK_SIDE.tips:
Elbow under the shoulder.
Push the hip up, don't let it drop.
Do both sides.

DEAD_BUG.description: On your back, arms up to the ceiling, knees at 90°: stretch out one arm and the opposite leg together.
DEAD_BUG.tips:
The lower back stays on the floor.
Slowly, breathing out as you stretch.
Alternate sides.

BIRD_DOG.description: On all fours, stretch one arm forward and the opposite leg back, then return.
BIRD_DOG.tips:
The back stays flat, like a table.
Look at the floor, neck in line.
Hold a second when stretched.

CRUNCH.description: On your back, knees bent, curl the upper back to lift the shoulders off the floor.
CRUNCH.tips:
Don't pull on your neck.
The lower back stays down.
Breathe out going up, come down slowly.

SUPERMAN.description: Lying on your front, lift your straight arms and your legs together.
SUPERMAN.tips:
Lift smoothly, just a few centimetres.
Look at the floor.
Squeeze your glutes.

PALLOF_PRESS.description: Side-on to the band's anchor, hands at the chest, push the arms out without letting yourself turn.
PALLOF_PRESS.tips:
The chest keeps facing forward: you resist the twist.
Feet hip-width, knees soft.
Do both sides.

EXTERNAL_ROTATION.description: Elbow against your side and bent at 90°, swing the forearm outwards.
EXTERNAL_ROTATION.tips:
The elbow stays at your side (a rolled towel helps).
Slowly, without shrugging.
Light load: it is a stabilising muscle.

INTERNAL_ROTATION.description: Elbow against your side and bent at 90°, bring the forearm in to your stomach.
INTERNAL_ROTATION.tips:
The elbow stays at your side.
Keep the shoulder low.
Slow return outwards.

LATERAL_RAISE.description: Standing, arms by your sides, raise them out to the sides up to horizontal.
LATERAL_RAISE.tips:
Elbows slightly bent.
No higher than the shoulders.
Lower slowly, without swinging.

FRONT_RAISE.description: Standing, raise your straight arms in front of you up to shoulder height.
FRONT_RAISE.tips:
Keep your back straight, don't lean back.
No swing.
Controlled lowering.

FACE_PULL.description: Facing a high anchor, pull the band towards your face, elbows out wide.
FACE_PULL.tips:
Elbows high, at shoulder height.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end.
Don't arch your back.

Y_T_W.description: Lying on your front, lift your arms into a Y, then a T, then a W.
Y_T_W.tips:
Thumbs to the ceiling.
Squeeze the shoulder blades in each position.
Small slow moves, no load at first.

SHOULDER_PRESS.description: Standing or seated, hands at shoulder height, press up to straight arms.
SHOULDER_PRESS.tips:
Brace your core, don't arch.
Press straight up, above your head.
Lower slowly to the shoulders.

BAND_ROW.description: Facing the anchor, pull the band to your lower ribs, elbows close to the body.
BAND_ROW.tips:
Start by squeezing the shoulder blades.
Shoulders low, away from the ears.
Slow return, arms almost straight.

DUMBBELL_ROW.description: One hand and one knee on a bench, back flat, pull the dumbbell to your hip.
DUMBBELL_ROW.tips:
The back stays flat and still.
Pull with the back: the elbow passes close to the body.
Do both sides.

BAND_PULL_APART.description: Arms straight in front, the band between your hands, pull it apart to your chest.
BAND_PULL_APART.tips:
Squeeze the shoulder blades.
Arms straight, shoulders low.
Controlled return.

REVERSE_FLY.description: Bent forward, back flat, open your arms out to the sides.
REVERSE_FLY.tips:
Elbows slightly bent.
Light load: these are the back-of-shoulder muscles.
No swing, back still.

PULL_UP.description: Hanging from a bar, pull yourself up until your chin passes the bar.
PULL_UP.tips:
Start by pulling the shoulders down.
No leg swing.
Lower to almost straight arms. A band helps at first.

PUSH_UP.description: On hands and toes, body braced, lower your chest to the floor and push back up.
PUSH_UP.tips:
Hands slightly wider than the shoulders.
The body stays straight, hips included.
On your knees to start with.

TRICEPS_DIP.description: Hands on the edge of a bench behind you, bend the elbows to lower yourself, then push back up.
TRICEPS_DIP.tips:
Elbows go back, not out.
Back close to the bench.
No lower than elbows at 90°.

BICEPS_CURL.description: Standing, arms by your sides, bend the elbows to bring your hands up to your shoulders.
BICEPS_CURL.tips:
The elbows stay against the body.
No swing from the back.
Slow lowering.

WRIST_CURL.description: Forearm resting, wrist over the edge, bend and straighten the wrist.
WRIST_CURL.tips:
Only the wrist moves.
Light load, full range.
Useful for the bow hand and the string hand.

FARMER_CARRY.description: A weight in each hand, walk, standing tall and braced.
FARMER_CARRY.tips:
Shoulders low and back.
Short steps, the body stays upright.
Grip the handles tight.

SQUAT.description: Feet shoulder-width apart, bend your legs as if sitting down, then stand back up.
SQUAT.tips:
Weight on your heels.
Knees in line with the feet.
Back straight, chest open.

LUNGE.description: A long step forward, lower the back knee towards the floor, then come back.
LUNGE.tips:
The front knee stays above the ankle.
Upper body upright.
Alternate legs.

WALL_SIT.description: Back against a wall, slide down until your thighs are level, and hold.
WALL_SIT.tips:
Knees at 90°, above the ankles.
Your whole back against the wall.
Breathe calmly.

CALF_RAISE.description: Standing, rise up onto your toes, then lower.
CALF_RAISE.tips:
Rise as high as you can.
Lower slowly.
On a step for more range.

GLUTE_BRIDGE.description: On your back, knees bent, lift your hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up.
GLUTE_BRIDGE.tips:
Push through your heels.
Squeeze the glutes at the top.
Don't arch your lower back.

SINGLE_LEG_BALANCE.description: Standing on one leg, the other knee raised, hold your balance.
SINGLE_LEG_BALANCE.tips:
Fix a point in front of you.
Standing knee slightly bent.
Harder with eyes closed or on a cushion.

ANCHOR_HOLD.description: With a light bow or a band, draw to your anchor and hold the position.
ANCHOR_HOLD.tips:
Keep your shooting posture: shoulders low, alignment.
Hold with the back, not the arm.
A lighter bow than your shooting bow.

BAND_DRAW.description: With a band, repeat your draw to anchor, then let it back slowly.
BAND_DRAW.tips:
The same move as on the shooting line.
Shoulder blades closing during the draw.
Controlled return, don't let go of the band.

SCAPULAR_SETTING.description: Arms straight in front, squeeze then spread the shoulder blades, without bending the elbows.
SCAPULAR_SETTING.tips:
Only the shoulder blades move.
Shoulders low.
Slowly: this is your draw's setup.

BOW_ARM_HOLD.description: Bow arm straight in front at shoulder height, hold it, with a light weight or a band.
BOW_ARM_HOLD.tips:
Shoulder low, pushing towards the target.
Elbow turned slightly out.
Light load, long hold.
